entries.definition: The top part of your body, where your eyes, ears, and mouth are.
entries.example: My head hurts today.

entries.definition: One of the two body parts you use to see.
entries.example: My left eye hurts in bright light.

entries.definition: One of the two body parts you use to hear.
entries.example: She has a pain in her left ear.

entries.definition: One of the hard white parts in your mouth that you use to bite.
entries.example: I brush each tooth at night.

entries.definition: The body part at the end of your arm, with fingers.
entries.example: Wash your right hand before you eat.

entries.definition: The long body part between your shoulder and your hand.
entries.example: I hurt my arm at school.

entries.definition: The long body part you stand and walk on.
entries.example: His leg is tired after the walk.

entries.definition: The body part at the end of your leg that you stand on.
entries.example: My left foot hurts after the walk.

entries.definition: The soft front part of your body where food goes after you eat.
entries.example: My stomach hurts after lunch.

entries.definition: A person whose job is to help sick people get better.
entries.example: I see a doctor when I am very sick.

entries.definition: A place where doctors and nurses treat people who are ill or hurt.
entries.example: She is in the hospital.

entries.definition: Something you take, often a liquid or a pill, to treat an illness.
entries.example: This medicine is for a cough.

entries.definition: Not well in your body, so you cannot do normal things.
entries.example: I am sick, so I stay in bed.

entries.definition: The bad feeling you have when part of your body hurts.
entries.example: I have a pain in my tooth.

entries.definition: A person trained to care for sick or hurt people, often in a hospital.
entries.example: The nurse checks my arm.

entries.definition: To push air from your throat suddenly, often because you are ill.
entries.example: I cough at night when I have a cold.

entries.definition: A higher body temperature than normal, usually because you are ill.
entries.example: The child has a fever.

entries.definition: A pain in your head that lasts for a while.
entries.example: I have a headache, so the room is too bright.

entries.definition: Said when your nose is blocked and you cough, but you are not seriously ill.
entries.example: I have a cold, so I drink hot tea.

entries.definition: A simple way to say your body feels ill.
entries.example: I do not feel well. I want to go home.

entries.definition: To telephone a doctor because someone needs medical help.
entries.example: Please call a doctor. He has a high fever.

entries.definition: An instruction a doctor or dentist gives so they can look inside.
entries.example: Open your mouth, please.

entries.definition: An instruction to swallow or use a treatment.
entries.example: Take this medicine after breakfast.

entries.definition: A throat that hurts, often when you swallow.
entries.example: I have a sore throat and a cough.

entries.definition: To visit a doctor for advice or treatment.
entries.example: You should see a doctor about that pain.

entries.definition: To sense that your body is unwell, sometimes that you may vomit.
entries.example: I feel sick in the car.

entries.definition: Pain in the part of your body behind your chest and stomach.
entries.example: Sitting all day gives me back pain.
